case_title: Nitinbhai Saevatilal Shah & Another v. Manubhai Manjibhai Panchal & Another
statutory_provisions: Negotiable Instruments Act s.138; Code of Criminal Procedure s.326, s.461, s.465
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.138 of the Act and sentenced to simple imprisonment for three months with a fine of Rs. 3,000/-
neutral_facts: The complainant, who was engaged in business, alleged that the accused had borrowed a sum of money and failed to repay it by dishonoring a cheque. The complainant presented the cheque for realization, which was dishonored due to insufficient funds. A demand notice was served, but the accused failed to pay the amount within the stipulated time. The complainant filed a complaint against the accused, leading to the registration of a summary case. The initial magistrate recorded evidence and was subsequently transferred. The successor magistrate proceeded with the trial based on the evidence recorded by the predecessor. The accused did not present any defense evidence, but one of them claimed that the cheque was signed under duress. The magistrate convicted both accused under the relevant statutory provision and imposed a sentence of imprisonment and a fine. The conviction was upheld by the appellate court, but the sentence for the company was set aside. The case was remanded for a retrial.
